correctness.rationale: For the regular-octagonal norm, the angle modulus at unit separation is one minus one half of the square of the least possible norm of the sum of two unit vectors at mutual distance one. The package proof reduces the constrained polyhedral problem to active supporting facets for the two unit constraints and the unit-distance constraint. On each feasible one-dimensional branch, the sum norm is the maximum of finitely many affine functions, so its minimum occurs at a branch endpoint or a support-switch point. The exact Q(sqrt(2)) checker at the assigned package path exhausts all 512 active triples, rejects 32 inconsistent triples, finds 48 feasible branches, and certifies the global minimum 3-sqrt(2), with 32 equality branches. An independent direct substitution of the displayed witness gives unit norms for both vectors and their difference and gives sum norm 3-sqrt(2). Therefore the claimed value 3*sqrt(2)-9/2 follows exactly.
residual_risks: The result is specific to one two-dimensional polyhedral norm and the single separation value epsilon=1.
The finite exact facet enumeration is exhaustive only because the proof first reduces every optimizer to the enumerated active-facet branches.

originality.rationale: Du, Ahmad, Din and Li define the angle modulus of smoothness, prove general properties, and compute it for some standard spaces, but their complete accessible article does not give the regular-octagonal value. Current published regular-octagon results located in the search corpus compute other invariants, including the parameterized von Neumann-Jordan profile and the Chen-Liu-Li G_L constant. Those objectives do not imply the present constrained minimum: at the symmetric von Neumann-Jordan parameter the prior objective maximizes a sum containing the squared difference, whereas the angle modulus fixes that difference and requires the least sum norm. No inspected primary or published finding covers the displayed exact value.
residual_risks: An equivalent fixed-distance polygonal computation could exist under P-angle terminology and be poorly indexed.
